findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting a close whose config is unreadable records `gate_unreadable` (never `gate_off`), matching the anti-laundering requirement stated for it in the Direction.
evidence: Direction: 'recording it as gate_off would launder it into a policy choice' for gate_unreadable
AC3: 'Each of force_bypassed, local_source and not_certifiable is recorded as ITSELF and never as gate_off' — gate_unreadable omitted
gate_unreadable maps to `_commands/gates.py:79-87` fail-open path, an uncovered deliverable
findings.finding: The enum value `gate_unreadable` is defined in the Direction table as a distinct FAULT state that 'must not read as gate_off' — the identical anti-laundering requirement AC3 imposes on force_bypassed/local_source/not_certifiable — but no acceptance criterion exercises or asserts it.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (AC3) vs Direction enum table row `gate_unreadable`
scenarios: Config unreadable at close time; a later reader sees no attestation and cannot tell fault from policy because no test proves gate_unreadable is written distinctly
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC3 to include gate_unreadable, or add a dedicated AC: simulate an unreadable config and assert the close STATUS event / reduced state carries `gate_unreadable`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion closing a bug as duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated and asserting the close records `disposition`, distinct from `required`.
evidence: Direction: `disposition` maps to `close_precheck.py:441-446` DISPOSITION verdict that 'IS signed, but is not a completion PASS and must not read as one'
No AC references disposition, duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated closes
findings.finding: The enum value `disposition` carries distinct reader-derivation semantics in the Direction ('disposition + attestation present -> closed and signed as a DISPOSITION, not a verified completion') but no acceptance criterion closes a bug as duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated and asserts `disposition` is recorded.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria vs Direction enum table row `disposition` and reader-derivation list
scenarios: A bug closed as duplicate naming a live replacement; a reader must distinguish it from a verified completion but no test proves the discriminator is written
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: close a bug ticket with a disposition class naming a live replacement and assert the reduced state records `completion_expectation == disposition`.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how gate_off and gate_unreadable are told apart at the source, since gate_enabled() returns an identical False for both (gates.py:80-87) before _completion_precheck sees it — e.g. have gate_enabled return a tri-state / (enabled, fault) tuple, or re-probe config readability in _completion_precheck.
evidence: gates.gate_enabled returns bool: `return bool(getattr(load_config(cfg_root).verify, attr))` on success and `return False` on ConfigError (gates.py:80-87) — both gate-off and fail-open yield False
close_precheck.py:411-418 `if not gates.gate_enabled(...): return None` — a single return None for BOTH the genuinely-off gate and the unreadable-config fail-open, with no residual signal

Plan asserts 'close_precheck already distinguishes all six cases at the points cited above but discards the distinction' — but for gate_off vs gate_unreadable the distinction is destroyed inside gate_enabled, upstream of any point _completion_precheck could capture it
findings.finding: The plan claims _completion_precheck 'already distinguishes all six cases at the points cited,' but gate_enabled() collapses gate_off and gate_unreadable into an identical False return before _completion_precheck can observe the difference, so these two enum values cannot be produced without changing gate_enabled.
findings.location: Direction, 'How the value is computed and threaded' + gate_unreadable enum row
scenarios: Config becomes unreadable at close time; the plan intends gate_unreadable but the code path can only yield the same signal as gate_off
AC row requiring gate_unreadable to be recorded as a FAULT rather than laundered as gate_off
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step changing gates.gate_enabled (or adding a sibling) to distinguish 'disabled' from 'unreadable-fail-open' — e.g. return an enum/(bool, unreadable: bool) — and thread that into the gate_off vs gate_unreadable expectation selection in _completion_precheck.

findings.checklist_item: Name who computes not_applicable for idea->closed, since _completion_precheck is skipped on the idea path (transition_close.py:325) — e.g. have close_ticket default the expectation to not_applicable on the idea branch, or have transition_core derive it from current_status=='idea'.
evidence: transition_close.py:325 `if target_status == 'closed' and current_status != 'idea':` wraps the _completion_precheck call (line 360), so idea->closed skips it entirely and verified_result stays None
close_precheck.py comment at 316-319 confirms idea close skips the completion precheck 'entirely'
Plan: '_completion_precheck returns the expectation alongside its verdict, close_ticket passes it into txn.transition_core' — this data-flow has no source for not_applicable
findings.finding: The plan states _completion_precheck computes and returns the expectation, but the not_applicable (idea->closed) case never enters _completion_precheck — close_ticket guards the call with current_status != 'idea' — so no owner is named for computing not_applicable.
findings.location: Direction, 'How the value is computed and threaded'; AC 'idea -> closed records not_applicable'
scenarios: Closing an idea ticket (REJECT/DROP): the plan requires not_applicable be recorded but the function that supposedly computes the expectation is never called
findings.suggested_fix: State that close_ticket sets completion_expectation = not_applicable directly on the idea->closed branch (where _completion_precheck is not called) and passes it to transition_core, rather than relying on _completion_precheck's return for that case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how _completion_precheck distinguishes gate_off from gate_unreadable given gate_enabled returns only a bool (e.g. change gate_enabled to return a tri-state / out-param, or resolve the config directly in the precheck), so gate_unreadable is actually reachable and not laundered into gate_off.
evidence: gates.py:79-87: `try: return bool(getattr(load_config(cfg_root).verify, attr)) except ConfigError: print(warning); return False` — off and unreadable both return False
close_precheck.py:411-418: `if not gates.gate_enabled(...): return None` — the caller sees only the collapsed bool and returns None in both cases

Plan: 'gate_unreadable | the config could not be read and gate_enabled failed OPEN ... recording it as gate_off would launder it' — requires the two be separated, but does not specify the return-contract change that makes the fault observable to _completion_precheck
findings.finding: The enum defines two distinct values gate_off and gate_unreadable, but the cited computation site cannot distinguish them: gate_enabled returns a bare bool that is False for BOTH the gate-off and the config-unreadable (fail-open) case, so _completion_precheck has no channel to tell which occurred.
findings.location: Direction / value table (gate_off, gate_unreadable rows); 'How the value is computed and threaded'
scenarios: An unreadable config skips the gate; the close records gate_off, laundering a fault into a policy choice — exactly the outcome the plan says must not happen
findings.suggested_fix: Have gate_enabled (or a new sibling) return a tri-state (enabled / disabled / unreadable) rather than a bool, and map unreadable -> gate_unreadable, disabled -> gate_off in _completion_precheck.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where not_applicable is computed for idea->closed given _completion_precheck is bypassed for idea (e.g. derive it in transition_core from the existing from_idea flag), rather than only from the _completion_precheck return.
evidence: transition_close.py:325: `if target_status == 'closed' and current_status != 'idea':` guards the entire block that calls _completion_precheck (line 360) — verified_result stays None for idea->closed and _completion_precheck is not invoked
txn.py:251: transition_core itself derives `from_idea = current_status == 'idea'`, but the plan does not route the value's computation there
Plan AC: 'idea -> closed records not_applicable ... verified by a test' — requires the value be emitted on a path the stated compute-and-thread mechanism does not cover
findings.finding: The plan routes computation of the expectation exclusively through _completion_precheck ('_completion_precheck returns the expectation ... close_ticket passes it into transition_core'), but the idea->closed close never calls _completion_precheck, so not_applicable has no specified computation site.
findings.location: Value table (not_applicable row); 'How the value is computed and threaded'
scenarios: Closing an idea ticket: transition_core writes the STATUS event but the plan-specified producer (_completion_precheck) never ran, so completion_expectation is unset rather than not_applicable
findings.suggested_fix: Compute not_applicable inside transition_core using the from_idea branch (txn.py:251) when the threaded expectation is absent, and reserve the _completion_precheck-returned value for non-idea closes.

findings.finding: The recorded 'expectation' derives from gate_enabled(), which fails OPEN (returns False) on unreadable config, so a config-unreadable close records 'not expected' and remains indistinguishable from a genuine gate-off close — a state the Problem section explicitly lists as collapsed but the solution does not resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Either derive the expectation from a signal that separates fail-open-unreadable from configured-off (e.g. record the resolution outcome, not just the boolean), or amend the Problem/AC to state config-unreadable remains conflated with gate-off and why that is acceptable.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note that docs/event-schema.md:47 (STATUS row) does not currently document close_class; author the completion_expectation doc entry directly rather than mirroring a non-existent close_class docs precedent (the code precedent at txn.py:287-288 does exist).
evidence: docs/event-schema.md:47 STATUS row: 'Sets `status`; carries `current_status` ... and `parent_status_uuid`' — no close_class mention
txn.py:287-288 shows close_class IS folded into status_data as the real (code-level) present-only precedent
findings.finding: The plan cites close_class as a documented present-only precedent in docs/event-schema.md, but the STATUS event row (docs/event-schema.md:47) documents only status, current_status, and parent_status_uuid — close_class is absent there, so the named docs precedent does not exist even though the txn.py:287-288 code precedent does.
findings.location: Direction, 'following that field's present-only precedent'; AC6 (docs/event-schema.md target)
scenarios: Author writes the docs edit expecting to append alongside an existing close_class entry that isn't there

findings.finding: The completion_expectation enum omits the DISPOSITION close, a seventh distinct expectation that _completion_precheck already produces, and the plan's derivation table would misread it as a verified completion.
findings.location: Direction section, enum table (values `required`..`not_applicable`); AC-2 derivation table
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the enum with a seventh value (e.g. `disposition`) covering the close_disposition.verdict path, and correct the plan's 'distinguishes all six cases' claim to seven; the derivation table should map `disposition` + attestation to 'closed as a named disposition, not completion-verified'.

findings.finding: The completion_expectation enum vocabulary omits the disposition-close return case, which _completion_precheck actually produces and which is a signed close that is not a normal completion PASS.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a row to the enum table for the disposition close (e.g. `disposition` = 'a bug closed duplicate/not_a_bug/escalated with a live replacement; verifier skipped but the close is signed'), and add an AC asserting a disposition close records that value rather than `required` or `gate_off`.

findings.finding: The plan's AC-2 requires a reader to separate the three states 'reading only reduced state,' but the reducer fold site (reducer/_processors.py _fold_close_class / the STATUS processor at lines 274,301) and the reduced-state schema (schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, where close_class is registered at :187-190) are not enumerated as edit targets. The plan invokes close_class as its precedent and names only the txn.py STATUS-data write; it says 'reducer handling' generically without naming reducer/_processors.py, and the event-schema addition line lists docs/event-schema.md but not ticket_state.schema.json. Without folding into compiled state and registering it in ticket_state.schema.json, completion_expectation would not be readable from reduced state, which is exactly what AC-2 demands.
findings.location: Direction section ('reducer handling'; 'writes it into the STATUS event data next to the present-only close_class') and Event-schema addition line; AC-2
findings.suggested_fix: In the Direction / event-schema-addition bullet, name the concrete fold site (reducer/_processors.py, alongside _fold_close_class) and add schemas/ticket_state.schema.json (register completion_expectation as reduced state, present-only) to the edit set, so the field is compiled into state and readable exactly as close_class is.

findings.finding: The Problem section lists 'config unreadable -> gate_enabled fails OPEN (gates.py:79-87)' as one of the states that today collapse into 'closed with no attestation,' but the Direction enum provides no value for it. A fail-open close would presumably record `gate_off`, silently re-conflating a config-read failure with a genuine operator gate-off — the exact conflation this ticket exists to break.
findings.location: Problem section (fail-open bullet) vs Direction enum table
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `gate_unreadable` (or similarly named) enum value for the fail-open branch, OR explicitly document that fail-open records `gate_off` with a stated rationale that the reader accepts the conflation.
